title: The seal of King Hezekiah
subtitle: The Hezekiah Bulla (Ophel)

images.caption: Drawings of the two royal emblems used in Hezekiah’s time: the winged sun, which appears on his bulla, and the winged scarab.

p: A clay seal impression about a centimetre across, found in the Ophel excavations just south of the Temple Mount, in a refuse heap beside a royal building. It reads “Belonging to Hezekiah [son of] Ahaz, king of Judah”, around a winged sun flanked by two signs for life.

It is the first impression of the seal of an Israelite or Judean king found in a scientific excavation. Jar handles stamped lmlk, “belonging to the king”, with the same royal emblems, are widely linked to the years when Hezekiah stocked Judah’s cities for the Assyrian invasion (2 Chronicles 32:27–29).
facts: 2009, in the Ophel excavations, Jerusalem; identified in 2015
